Executive Order 12791 of March 9, 1992 (cited from its American Presidency Project mirror capture; original not yet held as an acceptable original, replace and re-check quotes) provides that Executive Order No. 12753 shall be superseded on the effective date of that order. EO 12791 states no separate effective date, so the first end is recorded as its signing date, March 9, 1992; the order's own stated period would in any event have run only to March 10, 1992 (inclusive reading). research_rationale:
Executive Order 12753 of March 8, 1991 (Nuclear Cooperation With EURATOM, 56 FR 10501) is one paragraph. Under section 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2155(a)(2)) it determines that failure to continue nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community would be seriously prejudicial to U.S. non-proliferation objectives, extends the duration of the statutory period to March 10, 1992, and provides that Executive Order No. 12706 shall be superseded on the effective date of the order. It is a one-year extension in a yearly series. Its own terms limit it to March 10, 1992. Executive Order 12791 of March 9, 1992 (57 FR 8717), the next link in the series (quoted from its American Presidency Project capture, a mirror transcription cited under the transcription ruling; the Federal Register text held in jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12791.txt has the same sentence), says that Executive Order No. 12753 shall be superseded on the effective date of that order, extends the period to March 10, 1993, and so replaced EO 12753 before or at the end of its own period. EO 12791 states no separate effective date, so its signing date, March 9, 1992, is used as the first end (the Federal Register disposition note held for this order likewise records that it was superseded by EO 12791 of March 9, 1992); the alternative reading is the order's own stated end of the period on March 10, 1992, one day later, which cannot make the first end later than that. Either way the order had no force by March 11, 1992, and nothing in the held sources shows any later revival. The U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog searches found no citation or action that continues EO 12753. Status recommended: no. The one-clause inventory is complete for this one-paragraph order.

EO 12791's supersession (March 9, 1992, effective date not separately stated) precedes or coincides with the order's own end of period (March 10, 1992).","independent_command_check":"There is no command in EO 12753 independent of the extension period: the sentence that EO 12706 shall be superseded on the effective date of this order is a one-time command spent when EO 12753 took effect, and the recital of earlier orders in the series commands nothing.","savings_check":"Savings state transferred_or_accrued: cooperation under the March 1991 to March 1992 period is accrued and the function passed to the successor extension orders; no savings clause in the order.","scope_check":"The order is a single paragraph with one clause covering the determination, the extension to March 10, 1992 and the supersession of EO 12706; there is no partial supersession: EO 12791 supersedes EO 12753 without limiting words."}

savings_residuals.reason: The determination and extension concerned the period ending March 10, 1992; cooperation carried out during that period is an accrued effect, and the function of extending the period continued only through the successor orders in the series (EO 12791 of March 9, 1992 and its successors), each making its own determination. The order states no savings clause and no right or duty of EO 12753 itself continued.
